key_result.coordinate: Definition 2.7, Observation 2.8, Theorem 2.9; arXiv v1 pages 4-6
key_result.hypotheses: alpha is a unit interval parking function of length n; alpha-up is split into blocks at every index i with a'_i=i
conclusions: A rearrangement remains unit interval exactly when it preserves the relative order inside every block.
The number of valid rearrangements is n! divided by the product of the block-size factorials.
key_result.proof_mechanism: The one-block word is forced to be (1,1,2,...,n-1). Different blocks occupy disjoint consecutive spot ranges, so their fixed internal strings may be interleaved. Induction on the number of blocks gives the multinomial count.
key_result.relation_to_selected_problem: Gives the ell=1 boundary structure and A[n,1]=Fubini[n]. It does not give a block theorem or unimodality for ell>1.

key_results.statement: tau[j,n](pi) is the longest contiguous suffix ending at j whose labels are at most pi_j; tau_n(pi) is the product over j; summing over all permutations gives T_n=(n+1)^(n-1).
key_results.proof_mechanism: Split a permutation by the position of its maximum to obtain recurrence 2.4, then solve the exponential generating-function equation g(z)=exp(z g(z)).

key_results.statement: For the circular linear-probing occupancy map A, the inverse fibre over an actual-location vector l has size equal to the product of the backward occupied-run lengths psi_k(l).
key_results.proof_status: Presented as an immediate observation after defining A and its fibres, not as a separately numbered theorem.

key_results.proof_mechanism: Partition by the final occupied run before the required empty cell, derive recurrence 3.1, and use the generating function from Section 2.

key_results.statement: For c cars and p linear spots, the success probability is f(p+1,c)/p^c=(1+1/p)^c(1-c/(p+1)); for c=p=n the number of successful preference lists is (n+1)^(n-1).

relation_to_selected_problem.direct: For a final car permutation sigma, tau[i,n](sigma) is the unrestricted number of possible preferred spots of the car in spot i. S1 states L[n-1](i;sigma)=tau[i,n](sigma).
relation_to_selected_problem.limit: Konheim-Weiss does not study maximum displacement bounds, exact maximum-displacement counts, or unimodality. Its product is the ell=n-1 boundary.

existing_document_assessment.finding: The final car-permutation orientation, run-length definition, truncated product, and dynamic explanation agree with the originals.
existing_document_assessment.defect: The section cites only S1 equations 2-4. It does not expose that S1 names Konheim-Weiss equations 2.1-2.2 as the unrestricted direct source and that the fibre interpretation appears in Konheim-Weiss Section 3.

existing_document_assessment.finding: Its warning that the unit-interval block theorem is not a theorem for general ell is supported by Bradt Theorem 2.9.
existing_document_assessment.defect: No factual defect found. The new record adds the direct proof source and its printed variable errors.

usable_results: The ell=1 block-shuffle characterization and multinomial decomposition.
The unrestricted parking-permutation fibre product and total count.

final_assessment.remaining_gap: Neither foundation proves or suggests a theorem that forces unimodality of exact maximum-displacement counts for all ell.
